title: The Blackwood Estate
intro: Blackwood Estate, the North Riding of Yorkshire. A November night in 1893. The county constabulary sent one inspector through the storm, and that inspector is you.
epilogue: The constable arrived at first light to find Arthur Blackwood waiting in the foyer with his hat in his hands, still insisting he had spent the evening reading in the conservatory.

arrival.title: The Foyer
arrival.prompt:
The front door booms shut behind you, and a bolt slides home on the far side. Through the oak comes the coachman's voice: "Sorry, Inspector. Mrs. Hale's orders. Nobody leaves until his lordship's killer is named."

Lord Edmund Blackwood lies dead in his study at the end of the hall. Three other people were in the house tonight: his nephew Arthur, his physician Dr. Crane, and the housekeeper, Mrs. Hale. Above the front door, a single carved lily, the Blackwood crest, watches you peel off your wet gloves.

foyer.title: The Foyer
foyer.prompt: Rain rattles the fanlight. A grandfather clock stands against the panelling, the gate ledger lies open on the hall table, and the study door at the end of the hall is ajar.
foyer.hint: Everything you need is in this house. Look at the clock and the ledger before you go poking at locks.

clock.title: The Grandfather Clock
clock.prompt:
The pendulum hangs dead still. Tucked under the clock face is a card in Mrs. Hale's neat hand: "Stopped at 9:47, when we heard the master fall."

It's an old household custom. When the master of a house dies, the clocks are stopped at the minute of death. The hands read 9:47.
items_revealed: Stopped clock — Mrs. Hale stopped it when she heard the fall: 9:47

ledger.title: The Gate Ledger
ledger.prompt: The gatekeeper logs every carriage in and out of the estate. Tonight's last entry is underlined twice: "Dr. Crane's gig departed, 9:15 p.m." Nothing has come or gone since. Arthur's horse is still in the stable.
items_revealed: Gate ledger — Dr. Crane's gig left the estate at 9:15 p.m.

front_door.title: The Front Door
front_door.prompt: Locked from the outside, and the oak is four inches thick. The key normally hangs on a hook by the umbrella stand. The hook is empty. You're not leaving this way until the case is closed.

study.title: The Study
study.prompt:
Lord Blackwood lies beside the hearth, a brass poker on the rug near his outstretched hand. The French windows to the conservatory are locked, and there is no key in them.

The desk drawer is fitted with a brass combination lock: four dials, each running 0 to 9. Scratched into the brass, in what looks like his lordship's own hand: "The house remembers the minute."
study.hint: "The house remembers the minute." Something in this house stopped at a very particular minute tonight.

drawer.title: The Desk Drawer
drawer.prompt: You crouch beside the desk and set your fingers on the four dials.

input_required.fail_text: The dials click round, and the drawer stays shut.

drawer.hint: The grandfather clock in the foyer was stopped at the minute of death. Four dials, four digits.

drawer_open.title: The Desk Drawer
drawer_open.prompt:
Zero, nine, four, seven. The last dial clicks home and the drawer slides open. Inside lie an unsent letter in Lord Blackwood's hand and a small iron key tagged "Conservatory".

The letter reads: "Arthur. I have seen the moneylenders' bills. On Friday I sign a new will, and you will receive nothing. E.B."
items_revealed: Unsent letter — on Friday Lord Blackwood planned to sign a new will leaving Arthur nothing

conservatory.title: The Conservatory
conservatory.prompt:
Wet glass, hot pipes and the green smell of ferns. Arthur told the coachman he spent the whole evening out here with a novel. His wicker chair is here, and so is the novel. But the oil lamp beside the chair is stone cold and full to the brim, and the novel's pages are still uncut. Nobody read a word in here tonight.

At the far end, a servants' passage leads toward the kitchen. Its door is fastened with a letter lock: four brass wheels, A to Z. Someone has chalked a reminder on the frame: "Same as the crest."
items_revealed: Arthur's alibi — the lamp is cold and full, the novel uncut: he was never in the conservatory

kitchen_door.title: The Servants' Passage
kitchen_door.prompt: Four brass wheels, A to Z. "Same as the crest."

input_required.fail_text: The wheels spin, and the bolt doesn't budge.

kitchen_door.hint: Look back at the moment you arrived. The Blackwood crest is carved above the front door.

kitchen.title: The Kitchen
kitchen.prompt:
The bolt slides back. Mrs. Hale and the cook sit at the scrubbed table with two cups of cold cocoa between them. The cook speaks first: "She's been at my side since half past nine, Inspector. We both heard the master fall."

Mrs. Hale lays the front-door key on the table and keeps her hand on it. "I took it from the hook myself. It goes to whoever names the one who did this. Not before."
items_revealed: Cook's statement — Mrs. Hale was in the kitchen from 9:30 until they heard the fall
Front-door key — Mrs. Hale will hand it over once you name the killer

accuse.title: The Accusation
accuse.prompt: Mrs. Hale's hand rests on the key. "Well, Inspector? Who killed Lord Blackwood?"
accuse.hint: Check each suspect against the minute of death, 9:47. Whose story falls apart, and who gained from the death?

wrong_crane.title: The Accusation
wrong_crane.prompt: "Dr. Crane?" Mrs. Hale turns the gate ledger toward you. "His gig went out through the gates at a quarter past nine, Inspector. Half an hour before the master fell." Her hand doesn't leave the key.

wrong_hale.title: The Accusation
wrong_hale.prompt: Mrs. Hale doesn't flinch, but the cook does, on her behalf: "She was sat right here with me from half nine, cocoa in hand, when we heard him fall. I'll swear to it in any court you like."

solved.title: Case Closed
solved.prompt:
"Arthur." Mrs. Hale closes her eyes.

The pieces fit. Dr. Crane's gig left the estate at 9:15, half an hour before the clock stopped. Mrs. Hale was in the kitchen with the cook when Lord Blackwood fell at 9:47. Arthur swore he was reading in the conservatory, but that lamp never burned tonight and his novel's pages are still uncut. And he had more reason than anyone: come Friday, he would have lost everything.

Mrs. Hale slides the key across the table. Outside, the rain has finally stopped.
